records.title: Work-up at the point of metastatic diagnosis
records.subtitle: Metastatic breast cancer · Breast
records.body: When feasible, safe and clinically useful, biopsy an accessible metastatic site to confirm the diagnosis and reassess ER, PR and HER2 rather than assuming that the primary tumour's profile is unchanged. If biopsy is unsafe, non-diagnostic or would not alter an urgent decision, proceed from the strongest available clinical, imaging and prior-pathology evidence and revisit tissue or liquid testing when it can change management. 1 Discordance between the primary tumour and a metastatic site can change the treatment pathway, including reassignment of hormone-receptor or HER2 status. A single historical assay should therefore not be treated as permanently dispositive when a safe, clinically useful reassessment is possible. Molecular testing is directed by receptor subtype and treatment history. In HR-positive, HER2-negative disease, test for alterations that select an accepted endocrine or targeted option, including PIK3CA , ESR1 and the wider AKT pathway when relevant. In triple-negative disease, test PD-L1 with the assay and cutoff linked to the intended checkpoint inhibitor, and establish germline BRCA1/2 status when it can alter treatment. Tissue and circulating tumour DNA are complementary when either alone is inadequate. 1 Endocrine therapy or chemotherapy first In hormone receptor-positive disease, endocrine-based therapy is preferred unless rapid tumour shrinkage is required because of immediately threatening organ dysfunction. Chemotherapy can produce a faster response but at greater toxicity and should not replace endocrine treatment merely because visceral metastases are present. Visceral crisis means severe organ dysfunction judged on signs, symptoms and laboratory studies together with rapid progression, not simply the presence of visceral metastases: the compromise must be severe enough that a slower-acting therapy would leave no opportunity for a second option at progression. Prior adjuvant endocrine therapy determines whether the disease is treated as endocrine-sensitive or endocrine-resistant. Endocrine-sensitive disease includes de novo metastatic disease and relapse well after completion of adjuvant endocrine therapy. Endocrine-resistant disease includes relapse during or soon after adjuvant endocrine therapy, or progression on endocrine treatment for metastatic disease. These definitions organise trial eligibility and sequencing but do not replace clinical judgement about pace, symptoms, organ function and prior exposure. 1

records.title: Hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative disease
records.subtitle: Metastatic breast cancer · Breast
records.body: The organising principle is endocrine dependence: suppress oestrogen-receptor signalling first, then add or substitute other mechanisms as resistance emerges. HER2-low expression overlaps this subtype rather than replacing it, and becomes an additional conjugate target later in the sequence. First-line endocrine therapy with a CDK4/6 inhibitor An aromatase inhibitor with a CDK4/6 inhibitor is the first-line standard, with ovarian function suppression added for premenopausal patients. CDK4/6 phosphorylates and inactivates Rb to permit the G1-to-S transition; inhibiting it produces cell-cycle arrest. Four placebo-controlled phase 3 trials established the class in the first line, each extending median progression-free survival by between 9 and 13.5 months. PALOMA-2 : palbociclib plus letrozole improved progression-free survival (24.8 vs 14.5 months, HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.46 to 0.72) but did not prolong overall survival at a mature 90-month follow-up (53.9 vs 51.2 months, HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.78 to 1.18), a result the investigators qualify for a between-arm imbalance in survival follow-up (N Engl J Med 2016;375:1925-1936; J Clin Oncol 2024;42:994-1000). MONALEESA-2 : ribociclib plus letrozole improved final overall survival over placebo plus letrozole (63.9 vs 51.4 months; HR 0.76) (N Engl J Med 2016;375:1738-1748; N Engl J Med 2022;386:942-950). MONALEESA-7 : in premenopausal and perimenopausal women given goserelin with tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor, ribociclib improved progression-free survival (23.8 vs 13.0 months, HR 0.55) and overall survival (not reached vs 40.9 months, HR 0.71) (Lancet Oncol 2018;19:904-915; N Engl J Med 2019;381:307-316). MONARCH 3 : abemaciclib plus a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor improved progression-free survival (28.2 vs 14.8 months, HR 0.54), with final overall survival numerically longer but not significant (66.8 vs 53.7 months, HR 0.80) (J Clin Oncol 2017;35:3638-3646; Ann Oncol 2024;35:718-727). PALOMA-2 MONARCH 3 MONALEESA-2 MONALEESA-7 Drug Palbociclib Abemaciclib Ribociclib Ribociclib N 666 493 668 672 Population Postmenopausal, treatment-naive for advanced disease Postmenopausal, treatment-naive for advanced disease Postmenopausal, treatment-naive for advanced disease Pre/perimenopausal, up to 1 prior chemotherapy line, no prior endocrine therapy for advanced disease Partner Letrozole Anastrozole or letrozole Letrozole Tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor, plus goserelin Early-relapsing endocrine-resistant disease allowed No No No Yes Objective response 42.1% vs 34.7% 49.7% vs 37% 43% vs 29% 41% vs 30% All four excluded visceral crisis, and all but PALOMA-2 excluded CNS metastases and inflammatory breast cancer. Choosing between the three inhibitors There is no head-to-head randomised comparison, and the differing survival results are a cross-trial discordance rather than a ranking: follow-up, power, population and drug biology cannot be separated. Ribociclib carries the strongest survival evidence, positive in both MONALEESA-2 and MONALEESA-7; palbociclib has shown none, but is the least demanding to monitor, without the diarrhoea of abemaciclib or the QTc prolongation of ribociclib. The practical differences are toxicity and monitoring rather than efficacy. Palbociclib Ribociclib Abemaciclib Schedule 125 mg daily, 3 weeks on, 1 week off 600 mg daily, 3 weeks on, 1 week off 150 mg twice daily, continuous Grade 3–4 neutropenia 66.5% 62% 23.8% Diarrhoea (any grade) 26.1% 38.3% 82.3% Transaminitis Not reported AST/ALT 20.1% AST 16.8%, ALT 17.4% QTc prolongation Not reported 3% vs 0.3% Not reported Premenopausal patients Premenopausal patients receiving endocrine therapy require ovarian function suppression or ablation. The endocrine partner and any targeted agent are then selected using the same disease biology, prior treatment and resistance framework used after natural menopause. 1 Premenopausal patients receiving a GnRH agonist were eligible in PALOMA-3 , supporting the fulvestrant–palbociclib combination in that population. MONARCH 2 also included premenopausal patients receiving a GnRH agonist, supporting the fulvestrant–abemaciclib combination. Aggressive disease without visceral crisis RIGHT Choice is the only randomised comparison of a CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy against combination chemotherapy. It enrolled 222 premenopausal and perimenopausal women with clinically aggressive disease, defined by symptomatic visceral metastases or rapid progression. First-line ribociclib plus an aromatase inhibitor and goserelin improved progression-free survival over investigator's-choice combination chemotherapy (21.8 vs 12.8 months, HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.43 to 0.87, P=.003), with far fewer treatment-related discontinuations (6.3% vs 27.0%) and immature overall survival (HR 0.92; J Clin Oncol 2024;42:2812-2821). Response rates were similar (66% vs 62%) and so was time to response (4.9 vs 3.2 months). It is phase 2, and the only randomised evidence on this choice short of visceral crisis. First line when the disease is already endocrine-resistant For a patient progressing during or within 12 months of adjuvant endocrine therapy whose tumour carries a PIK3CA mutation, INAVO120 tested a first-line triplet. Inavolisib added to palbociclib and fulvestrant doubled progression-free survival (15.0 vs 7.3 months, HR 0.43) and improved overall survival (34.0 vs 27.0 months, HR 0.67), the first confirmed survival benefit for a PI3K-pathway inhibitor in this disease (N Engl J Med 2024;391:1584-1596; N Engl J Med 2025;393:151-161). Objective response was 63% versus 28%. Where the tumour is PIK3CA wild-type, first-line treatment for endocrine-resistant disease is fulvestrant with a CDK4/6 inhibitor, with ovarian suppression if premenopausal. Deferring the CDK4/6 inhibitor SONIA randomised the timing of the class rather than the drug: both arms received the same aromatase-inhibitor-then-fulvestrant sequence, and only the position of the CDK4/6 inhibitor differed. At the primary report, first-line use did not establish superiority for second progression-free survival (31.0 vs 26.8 months; HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.03). Updated second progression-free survival modestly favoured first-line use (HR 0.82), but final overall survival did not (47.9 vs 48.1 months; HR 0.91), while first-line treatment caused more toxicity, exposure and cost (Nature 2024;636:474-480; JAMA Oncol 2026;12:375-383). The post hoc premenopausal overall-survival result is hypothesis-generating. SONIA weakens the assumption that every eligible patient must receive a CDK4/6 inhibitor immediately, but it does not settle sequencing for the whole class: both arms eventually expose the patient to the drug, and the design was palbociclib-dominant. Its second-line comparator was fulvestrant monotherapy, which is no longer what most patients receive at that point. Deferral is reasonable in selected patients: endocrine-sensitive disease relapsing more than 12 months after adjuvant therapy, or a patient wanting to avoid the toxicity, the cost, or the interruption radiotherapy to a symptomatic site would require. Endocrine monotherapy and the first-line alternatives In FALCON , fulvestrant prolonged progression-free survival over anastrozole in endocrine-therapy-naive advanced disease (16.6 vs 13.8 months; HR 0.80) (Lancet 2016;388:2997-3005). The larger estimate in non-visceral disease was exploratory and no interaction test was reported. In current practice, endocrine monotherapy is mainly reserved for selected patients in whom combination therapy is unsuitable or deliberately deferred. Second line: reading the first-line regimen Three questions settle the second-line decision: was a CDK4/6 inhibitor given, is there an ESR1 mutation, and is there a PIK3CA or wider AKT-pathway alteration. Fulvestrant is given at 500 mg intramuscularly as two 5-mL injections, one in each buttock, on days 1, 15 and 29 and then once monthly. 12 In the double-blind phase III CONFIRM trial, 736 postmenopausal women with ER-positive locally advanced or metastatic disease progressing after prior endocrine therapy were randomised to this 500-mg regimen or 250 mg every 28 days. The 500-mg regimen improved progression-free survival (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.68 to 0.94, P=.006) without increased toxicity. 13 At final follow-up, median overall survival was 26.4 versus 22.3 months (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.69 to 0.96, nominal P=.02), with no clinically important difference in serious-adverse-event profiles. 14 Finding Option Trial Evidence No prior CDK4/6 inhibitor Fulvestrant plus a CDK4/6 inhibitor PALOMA-3, MONARCH 2, MONALEESA-3 Progression-free survival across the class; survival with ribociclib and abemaciclib ESR1 mutation Elacestrant, imlunestrant or vepdegestrant EMERALD , EMBER-3 , VERITAC-2 (vepdegestrant) Progression-free survival; survival immature PIK3CA mutation Alpelisib plus fulvestrant SOLAR-1 Progression-free survival; no significant survival gain PIK3CA , AKT1 or PTEN alteration Capivasertib plus fulvestrant CAPItello-291 Progression-free survival; no significant survival gain PIK3CA wild-type after CDK4/6 inhibition Gedatolisib plus fulvestrant, with or without palbociclib VIKTORIA-1 Progression-free survival only Prior CDK4/6 inhibitor, no actionable alteration Switch endocrine partner and continue CDK4/6 blockade postMONARCH , MAINTAIN (Kalinsky) Progression-free survival Prior CDK4/6 inhibitor, no actionable alteration Everolimus plus exemestane BOLERO-2 Progression-free survival, in a population that had not received a CDK4/6 inhibitor HER2-low, chemotherapy-pretreated Trastuzumab deruxtecan DESTINY-Breast04 Progression-free and overall survival HER2-low or ultralow, chemotherapy-naive Trastuzumab deruxtecan DESTINY-Breast06 Progression-free survival only, survival immature; the ultralow cohort exploratory Germline BRCA1/2 Olaparib or talazoparib OlympiAD , EMBRACA Progression-free survival For a patient with primary endocrine resistance who is PIK3CA and ESR1 wild-type, second-line endocrine therapy may have less to offer, and chemotherapy or an antibody–drug conjugate is a reasonable alternative. VIKTORIA-1 is the qualification, having tested an endocrine-partnered regimen in prospectively PIK3CA wild-type disease after a CDK4/6 inhibitor. Where a CDK4/6 inhibitor was not given first line, adding one to fulvestrant improves progression-free survival across the class. PALOMA-3: palbociclib plus fulvestrant improved progression-free survival after progression on prior endocrine therapy (9.2 vs 3.8 months, HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.32 to 0.56, P<0.001); prespecified overall survival was numerically longer but not significant (34.9 vs 28.0 months, HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.64 to 1.03, P=0.09), reaching significance in the endocrine-sensitive subgroup (HR 0.72) (N Engl J Med 2015;373:209-219; N Engl J Med 2018;379:1926-1936). MONARCH 2: abemaciclib plus fulvestrant improved progression-free survival (16.4 vs 9.3 months; HR 0.553) and final overall survival (45.8 vs 37.3 months; HR 0.784) in endocrine-resistant disease (J Clin Oncol 2017;35:2875-2884; JCO Oncol Adv 2025;2:e2500052). MONALEESA-3: ribociclib plus fulvestrant improved progression-free survival (20.5 vs 12.8 months; HR 0.59) and overall survival (median not reached vs 40.0 months; HR 0.72) (J Clin Oncol 2018;36:2465-2472; N Engl J Med 2020;382:514-524). ESR1-mutant disease and the oral SERDs ESR1 mutations, chiefly D538G, Y537S and Y537N, develop in around 40% of patients with HR-positive metastatic disease at progression. Testing turns the mutation into a treatment variable rather than a retrospective explanation for resistance. EMERALD: elacestrant improved progression-free survival over standard endocrine monotherapy in ESR1 -mutant disease (3.8 vs 1.9 months; HR 0.55). Interim overall survival in the overall population was not statistically significant (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.54 to 1.04) (J Clin Oncol 2022;40:3246-3256). EMBER-3: imlunestrant beat standard endocrine therapy in the ESR1 -mutant subgroup (5.5 vs 3.8 months; restricted mean survival time difference 2.6 months, with no hazard ratio reported because the hazards were non-proportional) but not in the intention-to-treat population (HR 0.87, not significant). Adding abemaciclib to imlunestrant improved progression-free survival regardless of ESR1 status (9.4 vs 5.5 months, HR 0.57) (N Engl J Med 2025;392:1189-1202). VERITAC-2 (vepdegestrant): vepdegestrant, an oral PROTAC oestrogen-receptor degrader, improved progression-free survival over fulvestrant in ESR1 -mutant disease (5.0 vs 2.1 months, HR 0.58) with a higher response rate (19% vs 4%), while the intention-to-treat primary endpoint failed its prespecified boundary (3.8 vs 3.6 months, HR 0.83, P=0.07) (N Engl J Med 2025;393:556-568). EMERALD met both co-primary progression-free-survival endpoints in the intention-to-treat and ESR1 -mutant populations. EMBER-3 and VERITAC-2 met their mutation-defined endpoints but not their intention-to-treat comparisons. None reported a treatment-by- ESR1 interaction, so these trials do not prove that benefit is biologically confined to ESR1 -mutant disease. The medians are short, no survival benefit has been demonstrated, and the class includes both selective oestrogen-receptor degraders and a PROTAC degrader. Switching on molecular progression ESR1 mutations become detectable in ctDNA around 6 months before radiological progression, which raises the question of whether to act on the molecular event rather than wait. SERENA-6 tested that strategy in 315 patients. Those on a first-line aromatase inhibitor plus a CDK4/6 inhibitor were monitored with ctDNA every 2 to 3 months; on detection of an emergent ESR1 mutation without radiological progression, they were randomised to switch the endocrine partner to camizestrant while continuing the same CDK4/6 inhibitor, or to continue the aromatase inhibitor. Switching improved progression-free survival (16.0 vs 9.2 months, HR 0.44) and delayed deterioration in global quality of life (21.0 vs 6.4 months, HR 0.54), with immature overall survival (N Engl J Med 2025;393:569-580). Second progression-free survival was not significant (HR 0.52); photopsia and bradycardia were adverse events of special interest. The result establishes this monitored-switch strategy for the tested regimen and setting. Whether it improves survival or generalises to other drugs remains open. PI3K–AKT–mTOR-altered disease PIK3CA mutations occur in about 40% of HR-positive, HER2-negative metastatic disease. The four agents in this space differ in what they inhibit and in the population they were tested in. BOLERO-2: everolimus plus exemestane improved progression-free survival after progression on a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor by local assessment (7.8 vs 3.2 months; HR 0.45) and central review (11.0 vs 4.1 months; HR 0.38), but did not improve overall survival (31.0 vs 26.6 months; HR 0.89) (N Engl J Med 2012;366:520-529; Ann Oncol 2014;25:2357-2362). SOLAR-1: alpelisib plus fulvestrant improved progression-free survival in the PIK3CA -mutant cohort (11.0 vs 5.7 months, HR 0.65) without a significant survival gain (39.3 vs 31.4 months, HR 0.86) (N Engl J Med 2019;380:1929-1940; Ann Oncol 2021;32:208-217). Only 6% of patients had received a prior CDK4/6 inhibitor, which limits direct application after contemporary first-line therapy. CAPItello-291: capivasertib plus fulvestrant improved progression-free survival overall (7.2 vs 3.6 months, HR 0.60) and in AKT-pathway-altered tumours carrying PIK3CA , AKT1 or PTEN alterations (7.3 vs 3.1 months, HR 0.50), but final overall survival showed no significant benefit in either population (AKT-altered HR 0.83, overall HR 1.00) (N Engl J Med 2023;388:2058-2070; ESMO Open 2026;11:107440). Sixty-nine percent had received a prior CDK4/6 inhibitor. VIKTORIA-1: gedatolisib, a pan-PI3K/mTOR inhibitor, improved progression-free survival over fulvestrant in prospectively PIK3CA wild-type disease after a CDK4/6 inhibitor, as a triplet with palbociclib and fulvestrant (9.3 vs 2.0 months; HR 0.24) and as a doublet with fulvestrant (7.4 vs 2.0 months; HR 0.33) (J Clin Oncol 2026;44:1108-1119). Grade 3 neutropenia occurred in 52.3% with the triplet. INAVO120 is the only member of this group with a confirmed survival benefit, and it differs from the others in being a first-line, mutation-selected triplet rather than a later-line doublet. The class toxicity is shared, being hyperglycaemia, rash, stomatitis, diarrhoea and nausea; relative frequency separates the agents. Alpelisib: hyperglycaemia 64% any grade and 37% grade 3 or worse, the highest of the group; glucose requires active baseline and on-treatment monitoring. Inavolisib: hyperglycaemia 59% any grade but 6% grade 3 or worse, stomatitis 51%. Capivasertib: hyperglycaemia 16%, diarrhoea 72%, rash 38% with 12% grade 3 or worse. Gedatolisib: stomatitis 57% with the doublet, 69% with the triplet. Everolimus: stomatitis 56%, rash 36%, diarrhoea 30%, hyperglycaemia 13%, pneumonitis 12%. Continuing CDK4/6 inhibition beyond progression Two randomised trials support maintaining pressure on the CDK4/6 pathway after progression, provided the endocrine partner is changed. They do not support continuing an identical failed regimen. postMONARCH: abemaciclib plus fulvestrant modestly improved progression-free survival after progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor and endocrine therapy (6.0 vs 5.3 months, HR 0.73), the first phase 3 trial to show benefit from continuing CDK4/6 inhibition beyond progression (J Clin Oncol 2025;43:1101-1112). By blinded independent central review the medians were 12.9 versus 5.6 months (HR 0.55), and benefit was greater in patients who had received at least 12 months of the prior inhibitor. MAINTAIN (Kalinsky): switching to ribociclib with endocrine therapy after progression on a prior CDK4/6 inhibitor improved progression-free survival (5.29 vs 2.76 months; HR 0.57, P=.006) (J Clin Oncol 2023;41:4004-4013). This phase 2 result does not establish a class-wide sequencing strategy. The gain is under a month by investigator assessment in postMONARCH, which is statistically significant and of questionable clinical importance. MAINTAIN is randomised phase 2. Both changed the inhibitor or the partner, and the mechanism of benefit after prior CDK4/6 inhibition varies by drug and design, so pathway persistence does not mean every continuation strategy works. HER2-low and HER2-ultralow expression HER2-low means immunohistochemistry 1+, or 2+ with a negative in-situ hybridisation result. This level does not predict benefit from conventional anti-HER2 antibodies but can permit activity from bystander-capable antibody–drug conjugates. HER2-ultralow means immunohistochemistry 0 with faint, incomplete membrane staining. Most HER2-negative metastatic breast cancers fall in the HER2-low band. These categories identify treatment eligibility at low antigen expression rather than a distinct tumour biology. DESTINY-Breast04: in the HR-positive cohort of previously treated HER2-low disease, trastuzumab deruxtecan improved progression-free survival (10.1 vs 5.4 months; HR 0.51) and overall survival (HR 0.64) over physician's-choice chemotherapy (N Engl J Med 2022;387:9-20). DESTINY-Breast06: in chemotherapy-naive disease after endocrine therapy, trastuzumab deruxtecan improved progression-free survival over physician's-choice chemotherapy in HER2-low disease (13.2 vs 8.1 months; HR 0.62); the intention-to-treat cohort including exploratory HER2-ultralow disease also favoured trastuzumab deruxtecan (HR 0.64) (N Engl J Med 2024;391:2110-2122). The two do not read identically on the expression gradient. DESTINY-Breast04 found benefit flat across immunohistochemistry 1+ and 2+/ISH-negative, whereas DESTINY-Breast06's subgroup point estimates diverge by expression depth with no interaction test reported. Whether that is a real interaction, chance in an unpowered subgroup, or the difference between a post-chemotherapy and a post-endocrine population is unresolved. The assay itself is imprecise at this threshold. DESTINY-Breast06 misclassified several enrolled patients against its own central testing protocol, and its investigators call for splitting immunohistochemistry 0 into two clinical categories, against the current ASCO–CAP position that the existing categorisation suffices. TROP2 antibody–drug conjugates Two TROP2-directed conjugates have randomised data in this subtype after endocrine therapy, separated by payload and toxicity rather than by target. TROPiCS-02 : sacituzumab govitecan improved progression-free survival (5.5 vs 4.0 months; HR 0.66) and overall survival (14.4 vs 11.2 months; HR 0.79) over physician's-choice chemotherapy after endocrine therapy and prior chemotherapy (J Clin Oncol 2022;40:3365-3376; Lancet 2023;402:1423-1433). TROPION-Breast01 : datopotamab deruxtecan improved progression-free survival over investigator's-choice chemotherapy after endocrine therapy and one to two chemotherapy lines (6.9 vs 4.9 months, HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.52 to 0.76, P<.0001), with a higher confirmed response rate (36.4% vs 22.9%) and far fewer grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events (20.8% vs 44.7%); overall survival was immature (HR 0.84) (J Clin Oncol 2025;43:285-296). Sacituzumab govitecan's toxicity is irinotecan-class, chiefly neutropenia and diarrhoea; datopotamab deruxtecan's is deruxtecan-class, chiefly stomatitis, ocular surface events and interstitial lung disease. Neither has been compared with the other, and neither has been compared with trastuzumab deruxtecan, so the HER2-low route and the TROP2 route increasingly treat the same later-line patient without sequencing evidence. Germline BRCA-mutated disease PARP inhibition selects patients by germline genotype rather than by receptor phenotype, so its trials enrolled HER2-negative disease of both hormone-receptor subtypes. OlympiAD: olaparib improved progression-free survival over physician's choice of capecitabine, eribulin or vinorelbine (7.0 vs 4.2 months, HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.43 to 0.80, P<0.001) and roughly doubled response (59.9% vs 28.8%). Final overall survival was not improved overall (19.3 vs 17.1 months, HR 0.90) in an analysis not powered for survival and confounded by crossover, with a non-alpha-controlled signal in patients treated in the first-line metastatic setting (HR 0.51) (N Engl J Med 2017;377:523-533; Ann Oncol 2019;30:558-566). Grade 3 or worse adverse events were less frequent than with chemotherapy (36.6% vs 50.5%). EMBRACA: talazoparib improved progression-free survival (8.6 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41 to 0.71, P<0.001) and more than doubled response (62.6% vs 27.2%), with patient-reported outcomes favouring talazoparib. Interim overall survival was not significant (22.3 vs 19.5 months, HR 0.76, immature) (N Engl J Med 2018;379:753-763), and the final analysis was negative (19.3 vs 19.5 months, HR 0.848, P=0.17) (Ann Oncol 2020;31:1526-1535). Grade 3–4 haematologic toxicity was higher than with chemotherapy (55% vs 38%), reflecting greater PARP-trapping potency. Both trials support PARP inhibition in germline BRCA -mutated, HER2-negative disease but do not rank the agents. Neither trial included platinum in the control arm, so PARP inhibitor versus platinum remains untested. The two trials disagree on which receptor subgroup benefits more. OlympiAD's progression-free survival hazard ratio was 0.82 (95% CI 0.55 to 1.26) in hormone receptor-positive disease against 0.43 in triple-negative disease, whereas EMBRACA's ran the other way (0.47 and 0.60 respectively). Neither trial was powered for the comparison.

records.title: HER2-positive disease
records.subtitle: Metastatic breast cancer · Breast
records.body: HER2-directed treatment developed from the trastuzumab-plus-chemotherapy regimen tested in H0648g (pivotal trastuzumab) . Subsequent strategies added a second antibody, used antibody-drug conjugates to deliver a cytotoxic payload, or used tyrosine-kinase inhibitors with intracranial activity. Adding trastuzumab to first-line chemotherapy prolonged time to progression (7.4 vs 4.6 months, P<0.001), raised objective response (50% vs 32%, P<0.001) and improved overall survival (25.1 vs 20.3 months, P=0.046) in HER2-overexpressing metastatic disease (N Engl J Med 2001;344:783-792). Concurrent anthracycline and trastuzumab caused cardiac dysfunction in 27% against 8% with anthracycline alone, which is why the durable HER2 backbone became a taxane rather than an anthracycline. First line Dual antibody blockade with a taxane remains the standard. CLEOPATRA added pertuzumab to trastuzumab and docetaxel and improved independently assessed progression-free survival (18.5 vs 12.4 months; HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.75; P<0.001). Final overall survival also improved (56.5 vs 40.8 months; HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.56 to 0.84), with an 8-year landmark survival of 37% versus 23% and no added cardiotoxicity (N Engl J Med 2012;366:109-119; N Engl J Med 2015;372:724-734; Lancet Oncol 2020;21:519-530). Adding pertuzumab increased diarrhoea (67%), rash (34%), mucositis (28%) and febrile neutropenia (14%). PERUSE reports outcomes by taxane. In 1,436 patients given investigator-selected docetaxel, paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel with pertuzumab and trastuzumab, median progression-free survival was 20.7 months and overall survival 65.3 months at 5.7 years of follow-up, with objective response in 79% (Ann Oncol 2019;30:766-773; Ann Oncol 2021;32:1245-1255). Paclitaxel and docetaxel subgroups had descriptively similar progression-free survival (23.2 vs 19.4 months) and overall survival (64.0 vs 66.5 months), with grade 3 or worse neutropenia in 5% versus 15% and febrile neutropenia in 1% versus 11%. Grade 3 or worse diarrhoea was 9% versus 8% and fatal adverse events occurred in 2%. Taxane choice was not randomised and no formal comparison was performed, so paclitaxel is a practical alternative rather than a demonstrated equal. DESTINY-Breast09 challenges the standard directly. First-line trastuzumab deruxtecan plus pertuzumab improved interim progression-free survival over a taxane with trastuzumab and pertuzumab (40.7 vs 26.9 months; HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.71) (N Engl J Med 2026;394:551-562). Grade 3 or worse adverse events occurred in 63.5% versus 62.3%. Overall survival is immature; CLEOPATRA therefore remains the established first-line standard while survival follow-up matures. Maintenance intensification and hormone receptor-positive overlap After induction chemotherapy has controlled the disease, antibody therapy continues as maintenance, and in HR-positive disease an aromatase inhibitor is added. Two trials intensify that maintenance phase further. PATINA : adding palbociclib to maintenance anti-HER2 therapy plus endocrine therapy prolonged progression-free survival (44.3 vs 29.1 months; HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.96) (N Engl J Med 2026;394:451-462). Overall survival was immature (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.61 to 1.23). Grade 3 adverse events occurred in 79.7% versus 30.6%, grade 4 events in 10.0% versus 3.6%, and grade 3 or worse neutropenia in 60.5% versus 2.0%. HER2CLIMB-05 : the trial enrolled patients with HER2-positive, HR-positive advanced breast cancer who had no progression after induction and no active brain metastases. Adding tucatinib to maintenance trastuzumab and pertuzumab prolonged progression-free survival (24.9 vs 16.3 months; HR 0.641) (J Clin Oncol 2026;44:1597-1607). Subgroup estimates were descriptive and overall survival was immature. Both measure progression-free survival from the start of maintenance, not from randomisation to induction, and both have immature overall survival. The high absolute medians reflect a population already selected for at least stable disease on induction. HER2CLIMB 's benefit on CNS-specific progression-free survival does not reproduce at this line; the subgroup benefit reported here is on overall progression-free survival in patients with brain metastases. Second line EMILIA established trastuzumab emtansine after trastuzumab and a taxane, improving progression-free survival (9.6 vs 6.4 months, HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.55 to 0.77) and overall survival (30.9 vs 25.1 months, HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.55 to 0.85) over lapatinib plus capecitabine, with less toxicity (N Engl J Med 2012;367:1783-1791). It was the first antibody–drug conjugate shown to extend life in breast cancer and established HER2-directed payload delivery after trastuzumab and a taxane. DESTINY-Breast03 then displaced it. Trastuzumab deruxtecan against trastuzumab emtansine in the same setting produced a median progression-free survival not reached (95% CI 18.5 to not estimable) versus 6.8 months (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.22 to 0.37, P<0.001), with confirmed objective response of 79.7% versus 34.2%; overall survival was immature at the primary analysis (N Engl J Med 2022;386:1143-1154). On longer follow-up progression-free survival matured to 28.8 versus 6.8 months (HR 0.33) and overall survival to 52.6 versus 42.7 months (HR 0.73), with interstitial lung disease in 15%. Trastuzumab deruxtecan is the preferred second-line option. The first-line trials excluded patients relapsing soon after (neo)adjuvant therapy, and the window differs: 12 months for CLEOPATRA, 6 months for PERUSE and DESTINY-Breast09. A patient relapsing inside their trial's window should be treated as second line. Third line and beyond No evidence establishes the optimal regimen after second-line trastuzumab deruxtecan, and the historical third-line sequence has been overtaken by the drug's move into second line. The options divide by mechanism. Tyrosine-kinase inhibitors: HER2CLIMB: tucatinib added to trastuzumab and capecitabine after trastuzumab, pertuzumab and trastuzumab emtansine improved progression-free survival (7.8 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.71, P<0.001) and overall survival (21.9 vs 17.4 months, HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.88, P=0.005); among patients with brain metastases the risk of progression or death fell (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.34 to 0.69) (N Engl J Med 2020;382:597-609). The trial supports tucatinib-based treatment where intracranial disease is clinically important. NALA : neratinib plus capecitabine against lapatinib plus capecitabine improved centrally reviewed progression-free survival (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.63 to 0.93, P=0.006; 12-month rate 29% vs 15%, medians 5.6 vs 5.5 months) and duration of response, and fewer patients required intervention for CNS disease (cumulative incidence 22.8% vs 29.2%, P=0.043). Overall survival was not significantly improved (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.72 to 1.07; restricted mean 24.0 vs 22.2 months) (J Clin Oncol 2020;38:3138-3149). EGF100151 (lapatinib + capecitabine) : lapatinib added to capecitabine after anthracycline, taxane and trastuzumab roughly doubled independently assessed time to progression (8.4 vs 4.4 months, HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.34 to 0.71). Fewer patients had the CNS as first site of progression (4 vs 11, P=0.10), an exploratory, non-significant observation rather than evidence of established intracranial efficacy (N Engl J Med 2006;355:2733-2743). Antibody–drug conjugates: DESTINY-Breast01 : single-arm trastuzumab deruxtecan after trastuzumab emtansine in patients with a median of six prior lines produced confirmed objective response in 60.9% (95% CI 53.4 to 68.0) with median progression-free survival of 16.4 months (N Engl J Med 2020;382:610-621). Interstitial lung disease occurred in 13.6%, including four fatal events (2.2%). DESTINY-Breast02 : in a post-emtansine population, trastuzumab deruxtecan improved progression-free survival (17.8 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.28 to 0.45) and overall survival (39.2 vs 26.5 months; HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.86) over physician's-choice therapy (Lancet 2023;401:1773-1785). Drug-related interstitial lung disease occurred in 10% versus less than 1%, with two grade 5 events on trastuzumab deruxtecan. TH3RESA : trastuzumab emtansine against treatment of physician's choice after at least two HER2-directed regimens improved progression-free survival (6.2 vs 3.3 months, HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.66, P<0.001) and overall survival (22.7 vs 15.8 months, HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.54 to 0.85, P=0.0007), with grade 3 or worse haemorrhage in 4% versus under 1% (Lancet Oncol 2014;15:689-699; Lancet Oncol 2017;18:743-754). HORIZON-Breast01 : trastuzumab rezetecan improved interim progression-free survival over pyrotinib plus capecitabine (30.6 vs 8.3 months; HR 0.22, 95% CI 0.15 to 0.34; P<0.0001) (Lancet Oncol 2026, online ahead of print). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events occurred in 70% versus 63%; interstitial lung disease occurred in 3%, and overall survival was immature. Antibody re-engineering and retreatment: SOPHIA : margetuximab, an Fc-engineered anti-HER2 antibody, modestly improved progression-free survival over trastuzumab on the same chemotherapy backbone (5.8 vs 4.9 months, HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.98, P=0.03), with no significant survival improvement at the second interim analysis (21.6 vs 19.8 months, HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.69 to 1.13) (JAMA Oncol 2021;7:573-584). Its prespecified but non-alpha-controlled CD16A-158F genotype signal is hypothesis-generating and under prospective test. PRECIOUS : pertuzumab retreatment after progression on a prior pertuzumab-containing regimen improved investigator-assessed progression-free survival (5.3 vs 4.2 months, HR 0.76, one-sided 95% CI upper bound 0.97, P=0.022) but independent-review progression-free survival was flat (4.4 vs 4.4 months, HR 1.03). Final overall survival favoured retreatment (36.2 vs 26.5 months, HR 0.73, no P value since alpha was spent on progression-free survival) (Cancer Sci 2022;113:3169-3179; J Clin Oncol 2025;43:1631-1637). It is underpowered by design, single-country and open-label. Brain metastases Local therapy remains standard for active brain metastases: surgery, stereotactic radiosurgery or gamma-knife. Two systemic options carry prospective intracranial data. DESTINY-Breast12 : a prospective single-arm cohort of 263 patients with baseline brain metastases including active lesions, tucatinib-naive by design. Median progression-free survival was 17.3 months (12-month rate 61.6%) with confirmed intracranial objective response of 71.7%, the largest prospective dataset for trastuzumab deruxtecan in stable and active brain metastases (Nat Med 2024;30:3717-3727). Investigator-reported interstitial lung disease occurred in 16% of the brain-metastasis cohort (grade 5 in 2.3%) and 13% of those without (grade 5 in 1.2%), with no central adjudication committee. HER2CLIMB enrolled patients with brain metastases by design, about half the trial. In patients with active brain metastases, intracranial response was 47% versus 20%, CNS progression-free survival 9.9 versus 4.2 months, and overall survival 21.6 versus 12.5 months. Which of the two better serves brain-metastasis disease is untested, because DESTINY-Breast12 excluded prior tucatinib by protocol design.

records.title: Triple-negative disease
records.subtitle: Metastatic breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Triple-negative breast cancer is diagnosed by exclusion, which is why it lacks the endocrine and anti-HER2 pathways that organise the rest of breast oncology. Two biomarkers are read in parallel at diagnosis of advanced disease, and they select partly overlapping populations: PD-L1 combined positive score routes the first-line backbone, and germline BRCA opens a genotype-defined option that cuts across the receptor subtypes. First line at PD-L1 combined positive score of 10 or more KEYNOTE-355 is the standard. Pembrolizumab added to investigator's choice of nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel or gemcitabine–carboplatin improved progression-free survival (9.7 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.65, P=0.0012) and overall survival (23.0 vs 16.1 months, HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.55 to 0.95, P=0.0185) in disease with a 22C3 combined positive score of 10 or more (Lancet 2020;396:1817-1828; N Engl J Med 2022;387:217-226). The combined-positive-score 1-or-more population did not cross its hierarchical boundary (overall survival HR 0.86), and intention-to-treat overall survival was therefore not formally tested. Without a treatment-by-score interaction or a direct alpha-controlled combined-positive-score 1–9 estimate, 50 does not prove that benefit is biologically confined to a score of 10 or more. Immune-related adverse events occurred in 26.5%, most often hypo- and hyperthyroidism. IMpassion130 provided the first positive randomised progression-free-survival result for checkpoint inhibition in metastatic triple-negative disease but did not establish an overall-survival claim in its intention-to-treat population. Atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel improved progression-free survival in the intention-to-treat population (7.2 vs 5.5 months, HR 0.80, P=0.002) and more so in PD-L1-positive disease by SP142 immune-cell scoring at 1% or more (7.5 vs 5.0 months, HR 0.62). Because intention-to-treat overall survival was not significant (final HR 0.87, P=0.077), the PD-L1-positive survival difference (25.4 vs 17.9 months, HR 0.67) could only be reported descriptively (N Engl J Med 2018;379:2108-2121; Ann Oncol 2021;32:983-993). IMpassion131 then failed to confirm it with solvent-based paclitaxel instead of nab-paclitaxel. Progression-free survival did not improve in PD-L1-positive disease (6.0 vs 5.7 months, HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.60 to 1.12, P=0.20) and overall survival numerically favoured placebo (22.1 vs 28.3 months, HR 1.11) (Ann Oncol 2021;32:994-1004). The atezolizumab indication in metastatic disease was withdrawn. The candidate explanations were the taxane formulation and the corticosteroid premedication that solvent-based paclitaxel requires, but KEYNOTE-355 succeeded including with paclitaxel, which weakens that reading. The two assays do not interchange. IMpassion130 reads PD-L1 on immune cells by SP142 at a 1%-of-tumour-area cutoff; KEYNOTE-355 reads a combined positive score on 22C3. Within one disease, "PD-L1-positive" denotes different tissue depending on which drug is under consideration. ASCENT-04 (KEYNOTE-D19) compared sacituzumab govitecan plus pembrolizumab with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab in the same combined-positive-score 10-or-more population. Progression-free survival improved (11.2 vs 7.8 months, HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.84, P<0.001) with a longer duration of response (16.5 vs 9.2 months) and far less discontinuation for toxicity (12% vs 31%), while response rates were similar (60% vs 53%) (N Engl J Med 2026;394:354-366). Overall survival was immature, untested and crossover-confounded. Two qualifications govern how far this goes. The comparison establishes superiority over chemo-immunotherapy, not over chemotherapy alone, because the control arm was the KEYNOTE-355 regimen. The result rests on progression-free survival and response durability, with overall-survival data pending. First line when immunotherapy is not an option Most metastatic triple-negative disease is PD-L1-negative at a combined positive score of 10, and a smaller number of patients are ineligible for a checkpoint inhibitor through prior exposure in the curative setting or a coexisting condition. For this group first-line care was chemotherapy alone, and two conjugates have now beaten it. ASCENT-03 : first-line sacituzumab govitecan improved progression-free survival over single-agent chemotherapy in checkpoint-inhibitor-ineligible metastatic triple-negative disease (9.7 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.62, P<.001) and prolonged response duration (N Engl J Med 2025;393:1912-1925). Overall survival was descriptive without formal testing. Grade 3 or worse neutropenia was frequent in both arms (43% vs 41%); adverse-event discontinuation was less frequent with sacituzumab govitecan (4% vs 12%). TROPION-Breast02 : datopotamab deruxtecan improved progression-free survival (HR 0.57) and overall survival (HR 0.79) over chemotherapy in checkpoint-inhibitor-ineligible metastatic triple-negative disease (Ann Oncol 2026, online ahead of print). Objective response was higher, and adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 3%, including one grade 5 event. No head-to-head comparison with another antibody–drug conjugate was performed. Here the control arm genuinely is the standard of care, so the result can be stated plainly: both conjugates improved on chemotherapy. Datopotamab deruxtecan has proven survival where sacituzumab govitecan has not, but that difference reflects trial maturity and crossover rather than a demonstrated potency gap, and the two were never randomised against each other. Choose on toxicity signature. Germline BRCA-mutated disease and platinum OlympiAD and EMBRACA both enrolled germline BRCA -mutated HER2-negative disease, about half of which was triple-negative, and both are set out above. In the triple-negative subgroup OlympiAD's progression-free survival hazard ratio was 0.43 and EMBRACA's 0.60. The two do not agree on which subgroup benefits more, and neither was powered for that comparison. Neither trial included platinum in its control arm, and both excluded patients who had progressed on platinum or received it recently in the curative setting. TNT (CRUK/07/012) provides the direct platinum-versus-docetaxel comparison without establishing that all homologous-recombination-deficiency markers predict platinum benefit. There was no evidence of an objective-response difference between carboplatin and docetaxel in unselected triple-negative disease (31.4% vs 34.0%; absolute difference -2.6 percentage points, 95% CI -12.1 to 6.9; P=.66). In germline BRCA carriers carboplatin doubled response (68% vs 33%, treatment-biomarker interaction P=.01), with progression-free survival of 6.8 versus 4.4 months and no overall-survival difference in a trial where 56% crossed over (Nat Med 2018;24:628-637). BRCA1 promoter methylation, low BRCA1 mRNA and a Myriad homologous-recombination-deficiency score did not predict platinum benefit. Germline BRCA status selects patients for platinum. Broader assays of homologous-recombination deficiency do not. Pretreated disease ASCENT established sacituzumab govitecan in pretreated disease. It improved progression-free survival, overall survival and response over chemotherapy in the brain-metastasis-negative primary population; the final intention-to-treat analysis including patients with brain metastases confirmed an overall-survival benefit (11.8 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.63) (N Engl J Med 2021;384:1529-1541; J Clin Oncol 2024;42:1738-1744). Grade 3 or worse neutropenia and diarrhoea were common. This trial did not compare first-line regimens. TROP2 expression is not a selection biomarker, and TROP2 testing is not required before treatment. Benefit held across every immunohistochemistry quartile with no significant treatment-by-expression interaction, and across HER2 immunohistochemistry 0 and HER2-low tumours. The antigen directs the antibody to the tumour without selecting which patients respond. HER2-directed conjugates occupy adjacent ground. In the exploratory, unpowered hormone receptor-negative cohort of DESTINY-Breast04 (n=58), progression-free survival was 8.5 versus 2.9 months (HR 0.46) and overall survival 18.2 versus 8.3 months (HR 0.48) (N Engl J Med 2022;387:9-20). That cohort remains the only evidence for the HER2-low route in triple-negative disease, since DESTINY-Breast06 excluded hormone receptor-negative patients. Read across the disease, three randomised, alpha-controlled results carry a demonstrated overall survival benefit: pretreated sacituzumab govitecan, first-line chemo-immunotherapy at combined positive score 10 or more, and first-line datopotamab deruxtecan in immunotherapy-ineligible disease. DESTINY-Breast04's triple-negative cohort points the same way without the power to prove it. The rest are led by progression-free survival and response with survival still open.

records.title: Cytotoxic chemotherapy
records.subtitle: Metastatic breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Sequential single-agent chemotherapy is generally preferred. Choose among active agents according to prior exposure, residual toxicity, organ function, symptoms and patient preference; use combination chemotherapy selectively when a rapid response is required for immediately threatening disease. This framework is more durable than a universal drug ranking because prior regimens and toxicity constraints differ across subtypes and lines. 58 1

records.title: Special situations
records.subtitle: Metastatic breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Brain metastases outside HER2-positive disease. Local therapy remains the default for active brain metastases. No specific systemic regimen has sufficient prospective evidence to support a general recommendation to defer local therapy in HER2-negative breast cancer; choose systemic treatment by subtype, prior therapy, extracranial control and clinical-trial availability rather than blood–brain-barrier plausibility alone. 59

records.title: What neoadjuvant therapy is for
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Neoadjuvant systemic therapy does three things that adjuvant therapy cannot. It downstages disease in the breast and the axilla, allowing less extensive surgery, better cosmesis and fewer complications such as lymphoedema, and it can render an inoperable tumour operable. It tests the biology of the tumour in vivo. The presence and extent of residual invasive cancer at surgery is a strong prognostic factor for recurrence, particularly in triple-negative and HER2-positive disease. It converts that readout into a treatment decision: residual disease triggers post-neoadjuvant escalation. Moving chemotherapy before surgery has not been shown to improve survival. The EBCTCG neoadjuvant meta-analysis pooled patient-level data from ten randomised trials (4,756 women entered 1983–2002, median follow-up 9 years) comparing neoadjuvant chemotherapy with the identical adjuvant regimen. Breast-conserving therapy rose (65% vs 49%), 15-year local recurrence rose (21.4% vs 15.9%; RR 1.37, 95% CI 1.17–1.61, p=0.0001), and there was no significant difference in distant recurrence (RR 1.02, 0.92–1.14), breast cancer mortality (RR 1.06, 0.95–1.18) or all-cause mortality (RR 1.04, 0.94–1.15) (Lancet Oncol 2018;19:27-39). The local-recurrence excess is not simply an artefact of good responders skipping surgery. It was largest in the two trials that permitted omission of surgery (10-year RR 1.62, 1.20–2.19) but persisted in the other eight, where surgery was scheduled irrespective of response (RR 1.28, 1.06–1.55), with no significant heterogeneity between the two sets (p=0.19). The evidence base is largely pre-taxane and pre-trastuzumab, which limits how far the local-control penalty carries into current practice. The original randomised comparison is NSABP B-18 & B-27 . B-18 gave identical AC before or after surgery in operable disease (n=1,493 eligible): at 16 years neither overall survival (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.85–1.16, P=.90) nor disease-free survival (HR 0.93, 0.81–1.06, P=.27) differed, while preoperative therapy raised breast-conserving surgery (68% vs 60%, P=.001) (J Clin Oncol 2008;26:778-785). A significant treatment-by-age interaction for overall survival (P=.01) favoured preoperative timing under age 50 (HR 0.81, P=.06) and postoperative timing at 50 or older (HR 1.23, P=.07). B-27 then added preoperative docetaxel to AC. Pathological complete response doubled, from 13% to 26% (P<.001), with no improvement in disease-free survival (HR 0.92, 0.78–1.08, P=.29). Within both trials pCR was strongly prognostic (overall survival HR 0.32 in B-18 and 0.36 in B-27, both P<.0001). Despite this prognostic association, doubling pCR in B-27 did not establish a survival advantage at the trial level.

records.title: Patient selection
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Neoadjuvant therapy is mandatory in some patients and optional in others. Upfront inoperable disease: inflammatory breast cancer, and locally advanced stage III disease (bulky or matted cN2, cN3, or cT4). Operable triple-negative disease of T1c or greater (larger than 1 cm), and operable HER2-positive disease of cT2 or greater or cN-positive. These subtypes respond often enough for the readout to be informative, they receive systemic therapy in any case, and a non-pCR identifies a patient for post-neoadjuvant escalation. A large primary tumour relative to breast size in a patient who wants breast conservation. cN-positive disease likely to convert to cN0, which may permit less extensive axillary surgery when the pretreatment node has been documented and marked. A temporary contraindication to surgery, such as an unstable thromboembolic or cardiac condition. Pregnancy itself is not a surgical contraindication: surgery is generally the primary local treatment for operable disease, while systemic therapy and radiotherapy are timed around gestation in multidisciplinary care. 3 For small, clinically node-negative HER2-positive disease, upfront surgery often provides the pathological stage needed to select adjuvant treatment without over-delivering neoadjuvant therapy. Patient selection should be aligned with current stage- and subtype-specific treatment guidance. 4

records.title: Work-up before starting
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Core biopsy of the breast with placement of an image-detectable clip, so the tumour bed can still be identified if the tumour responds completely. Axillary ultrasound in cN0 disease; ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration or core biopsy in cN-positive disease to confirm involvement. 4 Clip placement in a pathologically involved node when post-treatment targeted axillary surgery is contemplated. Breast ultrasound. Breast MRI is not routine but helps define disease extent, including multifocal and multicentric disease. Systemic staging is selected by clinical stage, symptoms and findings rather than performed uniformly in every patient. 4

records.title: Assessment on and after treatment
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Clinical assessment during treatment should identify progression and preserve a feasible surgical plan; repeat imaging is used when it will change that plan or when progression is suspected. Imaging cannot establish pathological complete response, so the surgical specimen remains the definitive response assessment. 4 Axillary management after neoadjuvant therapy follows the pretreatment nodal status. cN0 before treatment: sentinel node biopsy at surgery. A negative sentinel node needs no further axillary treatment; a positive one is managed by axillary dissection. Axillary radiotherapy is not a general substitute for dissection and is used only where a population-specific guideline or trial pathway supports it. cN2–3 before treatment: axillary dissection. cN1 before treatment that remains ycN1: axillary dissection. cN1 before treatment that converts to ycN0: sentinel node biopsy with removal of the previously clipped node. These pathways require appropriate node retrieval and multidisciplinary review; surgery, axillary staging and radiotherapy are covered in the early breast cancer chapter. 4

records.title: Pathological complete response as an endpoint
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: The definition used changes what pCR predicts. In the CTNeoBC pooled analysis , an FDA-led pooled analysis of 12 neoadjuvant trials (11,955 patients, all subtypes), clearing tumour from both breast and nodes (ypT0 ypN0 or ypT0/is ypN0) predicted overall survival better (HR 0.36 for both) than clearing the breast alone (ypT0/is, HR 0.51) (Lancet 2014;384:164-172). At patient level pCR is a powerful prognostic marker. Defined as ypT0/is ypN0 it predicted event-free survival (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.43–0.54) and overall survival (HR 0.36, 0.31–0.42), most strongly in triple-negative disease (event-free survival HR 0.24) and in HER2-positive, hormone-receptor-negative disease treated with trastuzumab (HR 0.15). At trial level it is not a validated surrogate. Larger between-arm pCR gains did not predict event-free survival gains (R²=0.03, 95% CI 0.00–0.25) or overall survival gains (R²=0.24, 0.00–0.70), far below the R² of approximately 0.75 conventionally required. A HER2-positive re-analysis (11 trials, 3,980 patients) reproduced the same split inside a single subtype: strong patient-level association (event-free survival OR 2.64, overall survival OR 3.15, with OR above 1 favouring pCR) and weak trial-level correlation (R² 0.23 for event-free survival, 0.02 for overall survival) (J Clin Oncol 2023;41:2988-2997). A patient who achieves pCR therefore has a better prognosis than one who does not, but a regimen that produces more pCR is not thereby shown to save more lives. Response-adapted escalation is built on pCR; regimen selection is not settled by it. Residual Cancer Burden (Symmans) grades the non-pCR group that the pCR endpoint treats as one bin. In a pooled five-cohort single-institution validation (n=1,158, retrospective pathology review with prospective follow-up, not a randomised trial), the index was defined as continuous with predefined cut points of 1.36 and 3.28 (J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1049-1060). Ten-year relapse-free survival by class (pCR / RCB-I / II / III) was 86/81/55/23% in triple-negative disease and 95/77/47/21% in trastuzumab-treated HER2-positive disease. Two qualifications limit it. In HR-positive, HER2-negative disease the gradient was not monotonic (83/97/74/52%), with pCR itself entering the multivariable model as a paradoxical predictor (HR 5.03, 95% CI 1.60–15.78) on small numbers. In HER2-positive disease treated with chemotherapy alone it dropped out of the model, with RCB-II and RCB-III failing to separate (44% vs 47%). RCB index was independently prognostic in triple-negative (HR 1.92, 1.49–2.46) and trastuzumab-treated HER2-positive disease (HR 1.80, 1.26–2.59). It is prognostic only, and the authors call for external validation.

records.title: Triple-negative disease
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: The chemotherapy backbone and the carboplatin question Adding carboplatin to an anthracycline–taxane backbone raises pCR consistently; its survival contribution remains uncertain. GeparSixto added weekly carboplatin (AUC 1.5) to paclitaxel and non-pegylated liposomal doxorubicin over 18 weeks in the 315-patient triple-negative cohort. pCR (ypT0 ypN0) rose from 36.9% to 53.2% (P=0.005), and on the 2018 survival analysis 3-year disease-free survival improved (86.1% vs 75.8%, HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.34–0.93, P=0.022), with the overall survival gain not significant (Lancet Oncol 2014;15:747-756; Ann Oncol 2018;29:2341-2347). Grade 3/4 neutropenia rose from 27% to 65%, and the homologous-recombination-deficiency score did not predict platinum benefit. CALGB 40603 (Alliance) , a 2×2 factorial randomised phase 2 (N=443) on weekly paclitaxel then dose-dense AC, found carboplatin raised pCR in breast and axilla (54% vs 41%, OR 1.71, P=0.003) but at 7.9-year median follow-up did not significantly improve event-free survival (HR 0.94) or overall survival (HR 1.12) (J Clin Oncol 2015;33:13-21; J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1323-1334). The trial was underpowered for survival, so this is an unproven rather than a disproven benefit. Within the same dataset pCR was strongly prognostic (5-year event-free survival 85.5% vs 56.6%), and even minimal residual disease at RCB-I fared worse than pCR. BrighTNess , a double-blind phase 3 trial, showed that carboplatin increased pathological complete response and improved event-free survival versus paclitaxel alone, whereas veliparib added no pathological complete response benefit beyond carboplatin (Lancet Oncol 2018;19:497-509; Ann Oncol 2022;33:384-394). The event-free-survival comparison was secondary, so the data support carboplatin's contribution without a confirmatory survival claim for veliparib. The TMC TNBC Platinum Trial (Gupta) is the phase 3 survival test in 717 analysed women at one centre. Carboplatin did not significantly improve the primary 5-year event-free-survival endpoint (70.7% vs 65.8%; HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.62–1.03, P=0.081). The secondary overall-survival comparison was nominal and not significant (79.2% vs 75.6%; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.49–1.12, P=0.166) (J Clin Oncol 2026;44:9-19). The accepted evidence does not establish a pCR result or a menopause-based treatment interaction for this analysis. Together, the trials establish a consistent pCR increase but do not prove a survival benefit or support selecting platinum by menopausal status. The question is partly absorbed into current practice, since the chemo-immunotherapy backbone already contains carboplatin and its separate contribution cannot be isolated there. Chemo-immunotherapy KEYNOTE-522 is the standard for high-risk stage II–III triple-negative disease. In 1,174 patients it gave neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks with carboplatin–paclitaxel for 4 cycles, then with AC or EC for 4 cycles, then adjuvant pembrolizumab for 9 cycles, against the same chemotherapy with placebo (N Engl J Med 2020;382:810-821). Each link of the chain was formally tested against its own alpha boundary and cleared it. pCR 64.8% vs 51.2% in the first 602 patients randomised, a 13.6-point difference (95% CI 5.4–21.8), P<0.001 against a boundary of 0.003. Event-free survival at the fourth interim analysis, HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.48–0.82), P<0.001 against a boundary of 0.01034 (N Engl J Med 2022;386:556-567). Overall survival at the final analysis (median follow-up 75.1 months), whole-period stratified log-rank P=0.002 against a boundary of 0.00503, with deaths in 14.7% vs 21.8% (N Engl J Med 2024;391:1981-1991). The 2020 publication states that its confidence intervals were not adjusted for multiplicity and cannot be used to infer effects. No overall survival hazard ratio is reported: the 5-year survival pair of 86.6% vs 81.7% is a descriptive landmark, and the weighted hazard ratio of 0.66 is an unstratified non-proportional-hazards sensitivity analysis carrying neither an interval nor a P-value. Benefit was consistent across all PD-L1 CPS strata on the 22C3 assay. In advanced triple-negative disease, the CPS ≥10 population is the evidence-based selection group because its prespecified overall-survival comparison crossed the alpha-protected boundary; the trial did not establish biological confinement of benefit to that stratum. PD-L1 is therefore not tested to select immunotherapy in early disease. Grade 3 or higher immune-mediated adverse events occurred in 13.0% vs 1.5%. Subgroups defined by outcome are exploratory, carry no alpha and were not tested against each other. In the no-pCR stratum event-free survival HR was 0.70 (95% CI 0.52–0.95), and by residual disease category 0.92 for RCB-1, 0.52 (0.32–0.82) for RCB-2 and 1.24 for RCB-3 (Ann Oncol 2024;35:429-436). Pembrolizumab was given before and after surgery with no arm stopping at surgery, so the neoadjuvant and adjuvant contributions cannot be separated. Two additional studies define the limits of the current regimen evidence. GeparNuevo (durvalumab) added neoadjuvant durvalumab to nab-paclitaxel then dose-dense EC in 174 patients, with no carboplatin and no adjuvant continuation. The primary pCR comparison was not significant (53.4% vs 44.2%, OR 1.45, P=0.287). At 86.4-month median follow-up, the prespecified secondary estimates favoured durvalumab for invasive disease-free survival (HR 0.56), distant disease-free survival (HR 0.41) and overall survival (HR 0.33) (Ann Oncol 2019;30:1279-1288; J Clin Oncol 2026;44:1580-1586). These nominal, non-multiplicity-adjusted phase 2 results are hypothesis-generating; they neither establish a checkpoint-class effect nor isolate or replace the neoadjuvant and adjuvant components of KEYNOTE-522. NeoPACT is a single-arm phase 2 (N=115, stage I–III) of pembrolizumab on an anthracycline-free carboplatin–docetaxel backbone for 6 cycles. pCR was 58% (95% CI 48–67) with RCB 0+1 in 69%, 3-year event-free survival 86% (98% with pCR vs 68% without), and grade 3 or higher immune-mediated events in 3.5% (JAMA Oncol 2024;10:227-235). There is no comparator, so no equivalence to the standard regimen follows from the cross-trial pCR similarity; SCARLET is the randomised test.

records.title: HER2-positive disease
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Establishing dual blockade NeoSphere established the contribution of dual HER2 blockade in the neoadjuvant setting. In 417 treatment-naive patients randomised to four cycles of one of four regimens, adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab plus docetaxel raised breast pCR from 29.0% (95% CI 20.6–38.5) to 45.8% (36.1–55.7), P=0.0141 (Lancet Oncol 2012;13:25-32). The chemotherapy-free dual-blockade arm still reached 16.8% and pertuzumab plus docetaxel 24.0%, so both drugs and the chemotherapy contribute. Grade 3 or higher events were mainly neutropenia and concentrated in the docetaxel arms. A fixed-dose subcutaneous trastuzumab–pertuzumab formulation is an administration option when otherwise appropriate. The loading dose is given over approximately 8 minutes and maintenance doses over approximately 5 minutes; repeat the loading dose after an interval of 6 weeks or longer. 15 Paring down the chemotherapy backbone The de-escalation sequence has removed the anthracycline and then the carboplatin, while leaving the taxane in place. TRYPHAENA (N=225) was a three-arm cardiac safety study of dual blockade with FEC then docetaxel concurrently, sequentially, or with anthracycline-free docetaxel–carboplatin. Symptomatic left ventricular systolic dysfunction was rare (2 patients during neoadjuvant treatment) and LVEF declines of 10 points or more to below 50% occurred in 3.9–5.6% across arms (Ann Oncol 2013;24:2278-2284). Descriptive pCR (ypT0/is) was high in every arm: 61.6%, 57.3% and 66.2%. TRAIN-2 tested the anthracycline directly in 438 patients with stage II–III disease. Adding anthracyclines to neoadjuvant paclitaxel–carboplatin plus trastuzumab–pertuzumab did not improve pathological complete response (67% vs 68%) or show an event-free or overall-survival advantage at 48.8 months; 3-year event-free survival was 92.7% versus 93.6% (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.63) (Lancet Oncol 2018;19:1630-1640; JAMA Oncol 2021;7:978-984). Anthracyclines increased grade 3 or worse febrile neutropenia (10% vs 1%), severe LVEF decline (7.7% vs 3.2%), and caused two acute leukaemias. neoCARHP removed the carboplatin. In a phase 3 non-inferiority trial (N=774), six cycles of taxane plus trastuzumab and pertuzumab were non-inferior to the same regimen with carboplatin AUC 6 (pCR in breast and axilla 64.1% vs 65.9%, difference −1.8%, 95% CI −8.5 to 5.0, P for non-inferiority 0.0089), with fewer grade 3–4 adverse events (20.7% vs 34.6%) (J Clin Oncol 2026;44:1587-1596). Non-inferiority rests on pCR alone; survival is immature. KRISTINE (TRIO-021) showed that replacing chemotherapy with T-DM1 plus pertuzumab reduced pCR in breast and axilla by 11 points against docetaxel–carboplatin with dual blockade (44.4% vs 55.7%, difference −11.3%, 95% CI −20.5 to −2.0, P=0.016), despite far less toxicity (grade 3–4 adverse events 13% vs 64%) (Lancet Oncol 2018;19:115-126). Event-free survival at 3 years was 94.2% with the chemotherapy regimen and 85.3% with T-DM1, driven by locoregional progression before surgery in the T-DM1 arm. The Neoadjuvant HER2+ therapy NMA (Villacampa) , a network meta-analysis of 46 randomised trials and 32 regimens (11,049 patients), supports most of that sequence and diverges on the last step: dual blockade plus chemotherapy was superior to trastuzumab plus chemotherapy for pCR, event-free survival and overall survival at the cost of more cardiotoxicity, and anthracycline-based chemotherapy was not more effective than anthracycline-free chemotherapy, but within anthracycline-free regimens carboplatin gave numerically better outcomes (Eur J Cancer 2023;190:112885). An antibody–drug conjugate front end DESTINY-Breast11 replaced dose-dense AC with four cycles of T-DXd before four cycles of paclitaxel with dual blockade, in 927 patients with high-risk disease (at least cT3 cN0, or cT0–4 cN1–3). T-DXd then THP improved pCR over dose-dense AC then THP (67.3% vs 56.3%, difference 11.2%, 95% CI 4.0–18.3, P=0.003), in both hormone-receptor-positive (61.4% vs 52.3%) and hormone-receptor-negative disease (83.1% vs 67.1%) (Ann Oncol 2026;37:166-179). The T-DXd-alone arm was closed early for inferiority (pCR 43.0%), so the taxane plus dual-blockade consolidation is still needed. Safety favoured the ADC front end: grade 3 or higher adverse events 37.5% vs 55.8%, all-grade left ventricular dysfunction 1.3% vs 6.1%, and drug-related interstitial lung disease low and similar across arms at approximately 4–5%. Grade 3 or higher interstitial lung disease occurred in 0.6%. Event-free survival is immature at 4.5% maturity (HR 0.56). Chemotherapy-free and response-adapted strategies Response-guided studies have tested chemotherapy reduction in selected lower-risk patients, using pCR to determine subsequent treatment. WSG-ADAPT-TP compared short-course T-DM1-based therapy with trastuzumab plus endocrine therapy in HR-positive, HER2-positive disease. Despite higher pCR with T-DM1, survival did not differ detectably on only 46 events and 19 deaths; non-pCR patients received mandatory chemotherapy (J Clin Oncol 2023;41:3796-3804). Among patients with pCR, 5-year invasive disease-free survival was similar whether adjuvant chemotherapy was omitted or given. WSG-TP-II compared trastuzumab–pertuzumab plus endocrine therapy with the same antibodies plus weekly paclitaxel in HR-positive, HER2-positive disease. pCR was higher with paclitaxel (56.4% vs 23.7%), while later survival estimates were untested (JAMA Oncol 2023;9:946-954; J Clin Oncol 2026;44:1974-1980). Most patients in the endocrine arm later received chemotherapy, so “chemotherapy-free” describes only the neoadjuvant phase. PHERGain-2 tested chemotherapy-free dual blockade in selected node-negative, centrally IHC 3+ disease. pCR occurred in 59.6%; non-pCR patients escalated to T-DM1 or chemotherapy plus T-DM1 (Ann Oncol 2026;37:837-848). Treatment-related adverse events were common, including one T-DM1-attributed pneumonitis death. The recurrence-free-interval co-primary endpoint is not yet reported, so pCR alone cannot establish preserved long-term efficacy. TRAIN-3 sent patients to surgery after an MRI complete response. Early responders had favourable 3-year outcomes, but stopping time was selected by response and toxicity rose with cycle count (Lancet Oncol 2026;27:349-360). This single-arm design does not establish that shortening treatment preserves efficacy against a fixed course.

records.title: HR-positive, HER2-negative disease
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy in HR-positive, HER2-negative disease is chosen mainly for downstaging or because systemic therapy is clearly indicated before surgery. pCR is less common and is a less useful treatment-selection readout than in triple-negative or HER2-positive disease. Regimen selection follows the same anthracycline- and taxane-based principles used after surgery, modified for cardiac risk, prior exposure and the need for downstaging. Complete germline testing when it can alter postoperative therapy. Routine neoadjuvant checkpoint inhibition is not established for this subtype. 4

records.title: Post-neoadjuvant therapy for residual disease
records.subtitle: Neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer · Breast
records.body: Residual invasive disease at surgery identifies a high-risk patient and triggers escalation rather than observation. In HER2-positive disease, KATHERINE randomised 1,486 patients with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane and trastuzumab to T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks or trastuzumab for 14 cycles. In KATHERINE, protocol-directed radiotherapy could be given during study treatment. In KATHERINE, at the final invasive disease-free-survival analysis, the HR was 0.54 and 7-year invasive disease-free survival was 80.8% versus 67.1%. In KATHERINE, at the second interim overall-survival analysis, the HR was 0.66 (95% CI 0.51 to 0.87) and 7-year overall survival was 89.1% versus 84.4% (N Engl J Med 2019;380:617-628; N Engl J Med 2025;392:249-257). Grade 3 or worse adverse events were more frequent with T-DM1 (26.1% vs 15.7%); grade 3 or worse thrombocytopenia occurred in 5.7% versus 0.3%. DESTINY-Breast05 compared T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg with T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks for 14 cycles in 1,635 patients with residual invasive disease who were node-positive at surgery or inoperable at diagnosis; radiotherapy could be concurrent or sequential. In DESTINY-Breast05, post-neoadjuvant T-DXd cut invasive recurrence or death by about half (events 6.2% vs 12.5%, HR 0.47, 0.34–0.66, P<0.001; 3-year invasive disease-free survival 92.4% vs 83.7%) (N Engl J Med 2026;394:845-857). In DESTINY-Breast05, T-DXd increased pulmonary toxicity: adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease occurred in 9.6% vs 1.6%, with two ILD deaths. Overall survival is immature. In triple-negative disease, CREATE-X (JBCRG-04) randomised 910 patients with HER2-negative residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant anthracycline and taxane to eight cycles of capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily on days 1–14 or to observation. Capecitabine improved 5-year disease-free survival (74.1% vs 67.6%, HR 0.70, P=0.01) and overall survival (89.2% vs 83.6%, HR 0.59, P=0.01) (N Engl J Med 2017;376:2147-2159). In the prespecified exploratory triple-negative subgroup, the disease-free-survival HR was 0.58 (95% CI 0.39–0.87). The treatment-by-hormone-receptor interaction was not significant (P=0.21), so the trial does not establish that relative benefit differs by hormone-receptor status. The trial ran entirely in Japan and South Korea, which qualifies the effect size rather than the strategy. For germline BRCA1/2 carriers, OlympiA eligibility includes both residual high-risk disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy and high-risk disease treated with upfront surgery. The early-breast-cancer chapter covers its efficacy and safety results. It enrolled both non-pCR patients and high-risk patients treated with upfront surgery, so it is response-directed-eligible rather than a residual-disease-only trial. Adjuvant pembrolizumab in KEYNOTE-522 is a different kind of post-neoadjuvant therapy: it is given regardless of pathological response, so it is response-independent continuation rather than response-directed escalation, and its separate contribution was never tested. Sequencing these escalations is unresolved. KEYNOTE-522 supports completion of its pembrolizumab course regardless of pathological response. CREATE-X supports capecitabine in residual HER2-negative disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in an immunotherapy-naive population, and OlympiA supports olaparib for eligible germline BRCA1/2 carriers. No trial has established concurrent or sequential overlap among these treatments; KEYNOTE-522 excluded adjuvant capecitabine. Selection therefore requires individualized multidisciplinary assessment rather than treating parallel trial eligibility as a combined regimen. Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibition for high-risk HR-positive residual disease is covered in the early breast cancer chapter.
